newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends sharply lower on NYMEX's lead.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends sharply lower on NYMEX's lead.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended sharply lower and near their session lows on Wednesday after NYMEX heating oil futures lost more than a cent a gallon at one point, traders said.

Crude oil prices held near unchanged in very chopping activity as traders balanced supportive U.S. inventory data with a well-established downtrend that has knocked 20 percent off prices in the last two months.
March gas oil last traded $3 lower at $165.75 a tonne, near its session low of $165 that is close to its eight-month bottom of $163.50.
At 1802 GMT, April Brent was up two cents at $19.47 a barrel, oscillating in a wide session range between $19.30 and $19.84.
"Heating oil in the States really was the leader of the whole market," an IPE floor broker said.
He said fund buying helped lift Brent futures toward their session highs and then some weaker longs started to bail out, creating vacuums in the market that exacerbated the volatility.
Some arbitrage buying from the U.S. started to filter into IPE Brent when the Brent/WTI spread widened toward $1.55-$1.60 a barrel, he said. That buying helped narrow it back toward $1.45.
